audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side read 'Zed' while content win[0..6] all read 'Xerath', the packet levelChart is Xerath on all seven rows, and every phases[N].why describes Xerath winning that stage ('level 1 Xerath is the longest gun in the lane', 'He farms at half HP forever or he doesn't farm').
audit.why: The row and the sentence under it argued with each other on all seven rows, and the two layers rendered opposite answers. Win rate is 53.77% over 3833 games in Xerath's favour, and Zed's longest reach is Razor Shuriken at 900 against Xerath's 1050 E and 1000 W.
audit.corrected: All seven sides to Xerath, matching the existing whys, the content layer and the packet. Level 6 rating dropped from 8/10 to 6/10 because Death Mark is a real threat window even in a stage Xerath wins on average.

audit.why: Spike structure holds: Lost Chapter, level 6 Death Mark (120/110/100s), first-item lethality roam window, and Zed's late one-shot threat. Zhonya's-at-assassin-6 advice is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent. (a) Death Mark makes Zed untargetable during the dash, so a pre-fired stun or R barrage passes through him — the stun has to land after he reappears. (b) Zed carries no hard CC at all: Shadow Slash only slows, so nothing in his kit can interrupt Rite of the Arcane's channel.
audit.why: Xerath's R is flagged 'channel — interruptible: any CC cancels it', and it is normally the first thing an assassin punishes. Against Zed specifically it is safe from interruption, which changes how freely you can channel.
audit.corrected: Both stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d and dosFull[2].d with real numbers: Living Shadow 20/19/18/17/16s, Shocking Orb 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s, Rite of the Arcane 130/115/100s.
sources: brief enemyKit E flags slow only

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and described the punishable cooldown as Death Mark. Living Shadow is the real one: 20s at rank 1 versus your 13s stun.
audit.why: Zed's escape and dodge tool is Living Shadow, not his ult; once it is spent he is a stationary target inside your range for seven seconds.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Living Shadow 20s/16s against Shocking Orb 13s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2). dontsFull[0].d was a name-swap template.
audit.why: Bodies contradicted their titles and carried no Zed-specific content.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten to their titles from Zed's kit.

audit.why: matchup-lint reported MISGENDER / COPY_PASTE_BLEED / COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT / UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE / HEDGING on these fields; cooldowns and ranges taken from champ-data/_kits.
audit.corrected: Pronouns matched to the enemy champion; bled trade text replaced with field-specific advice; cooldown lines given real per-rank numbers.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Check it before every step-up. - E Shocking Orb is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1 and 16s maxed — once he burns it, your 13s Shocking Orb outlasts him. - Death Mark's dash is untargetable, so a pre-fired stun passes through him; stun him after he reappears. - He carries no CC to break your channel.

edits.before: Zed spends Death Mark early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Nothing in Zed's kit interrupts a channel — fire your 130s R at his runback.

edits.before: That is Zed’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Past river his 650-range shadow puts him on you first.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: Contempt for the Weak adds bonus magic damage to his autos on a low-health target — at half HP his Q-E-R does more than the numbers you checked.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Zed wins by swapping to a Living Shadow inside your 1050, stacking Q and Shadow Slash on the mark, and letting Death Mark repeat it.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1 and your Shocking Orb is 13s, so E outlasts the swap — hold it for the dive and let Q and W do the chipping.

notes: content win[0..6] were already 'Xerath', so the side flips are unpaired by design — a before==after win[N] edit would be a no-op and would take the whole atomic chart group down. Every phases[N].why already described Xerath winning, so no why rewrites were needed and no row now argues with itself. diff stays HARD 8/10: winning the average stage and being one-shot-able at 6 are both true, and the difficulty rating carries that, not the chart. tradeBad still says 'the dash you bought it for' generically and is quoted verbatim in breakdown.trading and report[3]; left alone rather than fixing one copy of three inside the length band.
